title: DIPLOMA LEVEL : TOOLS IN DATA SCIENCE (COMPUTER BASED EXAM)

questions.text: THIS IS QUESTION PAPER FOR THE SUBJECT "DIPLOMA LEVEL : TOOLS IN DATA SCIENCE (COMPUTER BASED EXAM)" ARE YOU SURE YOU HAVE TO WRITE EXAM FOR THIS SUBJECT? CROSS CHECK YOUR HALL TICKET TO CONFIRM THE SUBJECTS TO BE WRITTEN. (IF IT IS NOT THE CORRECT SUBJECT, PLS CHECK THE SECTION AT THE TOP FOR THE SUBJECTS REGISTERED BY YOU)

questions.text: After a release, average API latency changes from 220 ms to 230 ms. The median changes from 120 ms to 125 ms, but checkout p95 latency changes from 400 ms to 2.8 seconds. Error rate is unchanged. What is the most defensible next action?
options: Treat the average as decisive and close the incident because overall latency barely changed.
Scale the database immediately because a tail-latency increase usually indicates database saturation under load.
Inspect slow checkout traces and correlated logs to identify where high- latency requests spend time.
Roll back every service immediately because an increase in p95 means the release slowed most requests.
questions.correct_answer: Inspect slow checkout traces and correlated logs to identify where high- latency requests spend time.

questions.text: An API's health endpoint returns 200 because the process can accept HTTP requests. All purchase requests fail because the production database credentials are invalid. The health endpoint does not test the database. Which conclusion is justified?
options: The health response proves the process and every dependency required by purchases are operational.
The process is live, but dependency readiness and complete purchase behaviour remain unverified.
The health response rules out server-side faults, so the browser is probably responsible.
The invalid credentials are harmless because a responsive process can reconnect automatically.
questions.correct_answer: The process is live, but dependency readiness and complete purchase behaviour remain unverified.

questions.text: Yesterday an API recorded 100 failed requests out of 1,000 requests. Today it recorded 200 failed requests out of 10,000 requests. Which interpretation is justified by these figures?
options: Reliability worsened because twice as many failed requests were observed on the second day overall.
Reliability cannot be compared accurately until the latency distribution is included in both reports.
Reliability remained unchanged because both reporting periods contained some successful and some failed requests.
The observed failure rate decreased from 10% to 2%, despite the higher absolute failure count.
questions.correct_answer: The observed failure rate decreased from 10% to 2%, despite the higher absolute failure count.

questions.text: A nightly scraper normally covers 100 pages. Tonight it fails after page 60. The pipeline marks every previously known item not encountered tonight as deleted. What is the integrity error?
options: Treat unseen items as deleted because each scheduled run represents a complete source snapshot.
Remove previous state after failure so the next successful run reconstructs the catalogue cleanly.
Preserve prior state because incomplete coverage cannot establish that unseen items disappeared.
Trust stored hashes to identify deletions even when later pages were never fetched.
questions.correct_answer: Preserve prior state because incomplete coverage cannot establish that unseen items disappeared.

questions.text: A vendor confirms that raw dataset version 1 contains an error and supplies corrected records. Which storage approach best preserves provenance?
options: Overwrite version 1 immediately and record the correction date so existing consumers need no path changes.
Preserve version 1, write a corrected immutable version, and record source, checksum, transformation, date, and owner.
Delete the original after validation so only corrected values remain available to downstream consumers and future runs.
Keep both files under the same mutable latest path so downstream loading remains convenient for every run.
questions.correct_answer: Preserve version 1, write a corrected immutable version, and record source, checksum, transformation, date, and owner.

questions.text: A public repository receives a pull request from a fork. The test workflow does not need deployment credentials. A separate workflow deploys trusted code from the main branch. Which design is safest?
options: Run untrusted fork code with deployment secrets because workflow masking prevents credential exposure in logs.
Give the test workflow repository write access so it can automatically repair the contribution before review.
Merge the fork first, then run privileged checks after its code enters the trusted main branch.
Test the fork read-only without secrets; deploy trusted main through a separately protected workflow.
questions.correct_answer: Test the fork read-only without secrets; deploy trusted main through a separately protected workflow.

questions.text: Tests pass, but the reviewed infrastructure plan says the production database will be destroyed and recreated because a field changed. What should happen next?
options: Manually edit the state record until replacement disappears from the displayed infrastructure plan.
Apply the plan because passing application tests establish that the infrastructure migration is completely safe.
Apply the replacement during low traffic and validate backup restoration after deployment completes.
Pause the release, investigate replacement, prepare recovery evidence, and require approval before applying.
questions.correct_answer: Pause the release, investigate replacement, prepare recovery evidence, and require approval before applying.

questions.text: A valid production API key was committed to a repository. A later commit removes the visible line. What is the most important immediate response?
options: Revoke or rotate the key immediately, then audit exposure and clean history where appropriate.
Delete the line in a subsequent commit and continue using the credential because main is clean.
Make the repository private and retain the key because future public access is blocked.
Trust secret masking because copied credential values should disappear from repository and workflow logs.
questions.correct_answer: Revoke or rotate the key immediately, then audit exposure and clean history where appropriate.

questions.text: A release candidate has passed tests and staging checks, but production traffic patterns are much larger and more varied. Which rollout provides the strongest risk control?
options: Rebuild the candidate in production using newest dependencies, then compare the result with existing staging evidence.
Route a small canary to the reviewed artifact, monitor thresholds, pause or roll back, then expand.
Shift all production traffic immediately, then inspect aggregate application logs after a full normal business cycle.
Disable rollout alerts temporarily, then evaluate detailed user reports before enabling production monitoring again.
questions.correct_answer: Route a small canary to the reviewed artifact, monitor thresholds, pause or roll back, then expand.

questions.text: An AI produces a fluent report containing several factual claims and a confident recommendation. The report will influence a business decision. Which review practice provides the strongest basis for trusting it?
options: Approve the report when its wording is confident and its recommendation reinforces reviewer expectations.
Require cited evidence, verify important claims independently, and record any uncertainty that remains.
Repeat the request until the same model produces several reports with similar claims and conclusions.
Provide additional background context and treat a longer, more detailed answer as stronger factual evidence.
questions.correct_answer: Require cited evidence, verify important claims independently, and record any uncertainty that remains.

questions.text: A downstream system expects one category from an allowed list and a numeric confidence score. An AI sometimes adds prose or invents categories. Which design is most reliable?
options: Parse the first two visible lines and ignore any fields or text that follow.
Emphasize the requested format in the prompt and store every response unchanged.
Add newly invented categories automatically so the system adapts without rejecting responses.
Validate responses against a schema and allowed values before accepting or using them.
questions.correct_answer: Validate responses against a schema and allowed values before accepting or using them.

questions.text: A support assistant answers questions from policy documents that are revised regularly. Answers must reflect the current published policy. Which approach best supports this requirement?
options: Rely on model memory because retrieved passages may contain conflicting policy versions.
Include every available document in each request so selection cannot ever exclude applicable evidence.
Retrieve relevant current passages, ground the answer in them, and expose citations or uncertainty.
Fine-tune once on the policy collection and treat its answers as permanently current.
questions.correct_answer: Retrieve relevant current passages, ground the answer in them, and expose citations or uncertainty.

questions.text: A support agent can read an order and issue a refund. Refunds above ₹5,000 require recorded human approval. Which control should enforce the rule?
options: Validate tool arguments and enforce permissions and approval in the application before execution.
Give the agent every support tool because unrestricted access reduces incomplete customer service.
Describe refund limits only in the prompt because the model will consistently remember them.
Treat a detailed customer message as sufficient authorization when the request appears urgent.
questions.correct_answer: Validate tool arguments and enforce permissions and approval in the application before execution.

questions.text: A service may scale to zero, restart, or replace an instance. It must preserve job status across those events. Which design is appropriate?
options: Store job state in instance memory and reconstruct missing records from service logs after restart.
Keep one minimum instance running because this guarantees local files survive every deployment.
Store durable state in a database or object store and treat compute instances as replaceable.
Return all state to the browser and trust the client to preserve authoritative records.
questions.correct_answer: Store durable state in a database or object store and treat compute instances as replaceable.

questions.text: An API returns HTTP 200 with the body [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p6_Im3.webp|inline] when a requested order does not exist. Which redesign gives clients and monitoring the clearest contract?
options: Return HTTP 200 with an error field because the server successfully produced a JSON response.
Return HTTP 500 with diagnostic details because any missing database record is a server failure.
Return HTTP 404 with a structured error body so clients distinguish absence from success.
Redirect to a general page because navigation is clearer than exposing an API error.
questions.correct_answer: Return HTTP 404 with a structured error body so clients distinguish absence from success.

questions.text: A browser frontend moves to a new origin. Its API request is blocked, while the same request succeeds from a command-line HTTP client. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Treat the API as offline because browsers and command-line clients use different network paths.
Allow the trusted frontend origin because browsers enforce CORS while command-line clients do not.
Treat command-line success as proof that the browser's new origin is already allowed by the API.
Add broader user permissions because CORS failures prove the caller lacks authorization to access that resource.
questions.correct_answer: Allow the trusted frontend origin because browsers enforce CORS while command-line clients do not.

questions.text: An application must sign a user in and learn the user's identity. With separate consent, it may read that user's calendar. Which distinction is correct?
options: Use OAuth for sign-in identity and OpenID Connect scopes for delegated calendar access.
Use OpenID Connect for both identity and unrestricted calendar access without separate consent.
Use OAuth alone as proof of identity and unrestricted permission to every provider API.
Use OpenID Connect for identity and OAuth scopes for delegated calendar access.
questions.correct_answer: Use OpenID Connect for identity and OAuth scopes for delegated calendar access.

questions.text: A faulty commit is already on a shared main branch and other developers have pulled it. The team wants an auditable undo without rewriting shared history. What should it do?
options: Reset the shared branch to an earlier commit and force-push the rewritten history.
Create a new commit that reverses the faulty changes while preserving shared history.
Delete and recreate the branch so contributors can pull a clean replacement history.
Amend the faulty commit and ask every contributor to rebuild work on the new version.
questions.correct_answer: Create a new commit that reverses the faulty changes while preserving shared history.

questions.text: A proposed GitHub Pages application must keep a private API key, execute server-side payment logic, and write directly to a database. What is the fundamental problem?
options: Static hosting lacks a protected server runtime for private secrets, payment logic, and database writes.
Static hosting cannot call external payment APIs or database services from client-side JavaScript at all.
Browser code can protect permanent private keys when source maps and developer tools are disabled.
Frontend environment variables remain private when injected only during the static site's build process.
questions.correct_answer: Static hosting lacks a protected server runtime for private secrets, payment logic, and database writes.

questions.text: A developer binds a laptop service to 0.0.0.0, but it remains inaccessible from the public internet. Which explanation is correct?
options: Binding to 0.0.0.0 gives the service DNS, a public route, open firewall access, and a trusted TLS certificate.
Binding to 0.0.0.0 assigns a permanent public address that bypasses routers, firewalls, and network address translation.
Binding listens on local interfaces; public access still needs routing, firewall permission, and often DNS and TLS.
Binding to 0.0.0.0 restricts the service to its own process and blocks every local or internet client.
questions.correct_answer: Binding listens on local interfaces; public access still needs routing, firewall permission, and often DNS and TLS.

questions.text: A system writes independent event records continuously. Operators want to append records and process them one at a time without loading one giant document. Which format property is most suitable?
options: Use JSON Lines so each line contains an independent record that can be appended, validated, and streamed.
Use one growing JSON array so consumers load the complete history before reading individual records.
Use a single JSON object keyed by event ID, rewriting the complete object whenever another event arrives.
Use daily compressed archives and rebuild the current archive whenever each new event arrives during operation.
questions.correct_answer: Use JSON Lines so each line contains an independent record that can be appended, validated, and streamed.

questions.text: One public server must expose api.example.com and docs.example.com over HTTPS while keeping both backend services on private local ports. Which component best fits?
options: Use DNS alone because it terminates HTTPS and forwards each hostname to a private application port.
Use a reverse proxy to terminate HTTPS and route each hostname to its private backend.
Use CORS middleware because browser-origin rules also map public domain names to internal service ports.
Expose each backend directly on a different public port and let clients select the correct port.
questions.correct_answer: Use a reverse proxy to terminate HTTPS and route each hostname to its private backend.

questions.text: An order request passes through an API, inventory service, payment service, and database. About 2% of requests fail, but the failing component is unknown. Which telemetry choices would best support diagnosis?
options: Monitor request rate, error rate, and latency separately for each service and route.
Label each metric with customer email so affected requests can be grouped precisely.
Write structured request logs with timestamp, service, trace ID, outcome, and error context.
Record complete authorization headers so failed requests can be replayed during diagnosis.
Propagate trace context so one request can be followed through every dependent component.
Record service start and stop events because process availability explains individual request failures.
correct_answer: Monitor request rate, error rate, and latency separately for each service and route.
Write structured request logs with timestamp, service, trace ID, outcome, and error context.
Propagate trace context so one request can be followed through every dependent component.

questions.text: An LLM feature's daily cost rises tenfold while request volume is unchanged. A cloud budget alert arrives several hours after the money has been spent. The team cannot attribute the increase to a feature, model, or request. Which additions would best identify and contain a recurrence?
options: Increase the monthly threshold and rely on fewer alerts to distinguish genuine cost incidents.
Record tokens and cost by request, feature, model version, and environment for attribution.
Enforce an application spend ceiling or provider quota that blocks calls after budget exhaustion.
Store complete prompts and credentials so finance can reproduce and verify every billed call.
Compare only the monthly bill with traffic because request-level details create unnecessary noise.
correct_answer: Record tokens and cost by request, feature, model version, and environment for attribution.
Enforce an application spend ceiling or provider quota that blocks calls after budget exhaustion.

questions.text: A product scraper runs hourly. Each product has a stable SKU. Title and price are meaningful business fields, while view count and fetch timestamp change on almost every run. Which design choices support correct incremental updates?
options: Generate a random ID each run so stale records cannot be mistaken for current ones.
Use the SKU as stable identity so repeated observations refer to the same item.
Include the retrieval timestamp in the hash so every collection event remains uniquely auditable.
Hash normalized title and price so changes to meaningful business values alter the digest.
Upsert by SKU and retain business values when the meaningful-content hash is unchanged.
Append each observation as a current record so no source value is ever overwritten.
correct_answer: Use the SKU as stable identity so repeated observations refer to the same item.
Hash normalized title and price so changes to meaningful business values alter the digest.
Upsert by SKU and retain business values when the meaningful-content hash is unchanged.

questions.text: A payment request times out. The service supports a stable idempotency key and a status lookup by that key, but the client does not yet know whether the payment completed. Which actions form the safest retry policy?
options: Assign a new idempotency key to each attempt so every retry is audited separately.
Repeat the request after each timeout without checking status or limiting total attempts.
Reuse the original idempotency key whenever the same logical payment is submitted again.
Treat the timeout as a successfully completed payment and never consult the service record.
Query the original key's status before deciding whether another payment call is necessary.
Create a replacement order so the retry receives a different payment identity for easier accounting.
correct_answer: Reuse the original idempotency key whenever the same logical payment is submitted again.
Query the original key's status before deciding whether another payment call is necessary.

questions.text: Which controls materially reduce CI/CD and container supply-chain risk?
options: Pin external CI actions to reviewed commit hashes so workflow code cannot change after approval.
Add deployment credentials during the image build, then delete them from the final container layer.
Build a minimal runtime image without tools or credentials, and run the process as an unprivileged user.
Deploy a mutable release tag so urgent fixes can replace the artifact without another workflow review.
Grant broad permissions to every workflow job so later deployment steps do not fail unexpectedly in production.
Deploy the reviewed artifact by immutable image digest or source commit rather than a moving label.
correct_answer: Pin external CI actions to reviewed commit hashes so workflow code cannot change after approval.
Build a minimal runtime image without tools or credentials, and run the process as an unprivileged user.
Deploy the reviewed artifact by immutable image digest or source commit rather than a moving label.

questions.text: A frontend and backend run in separate containers on the same application network. The backend also writes durable customer records. Which statements are correct?
options: Place durable records in a volume, database, or object store outside the replaceable container layer.
Use localhost from the frontend because it always refers to the application's separate backend service.
Reach the backend through its service name or internal address on the shared container network.
Keep records in the writable layer because replacement reliably preserves all container files by default.
Treat the image as live storage because it continuously records updates made by running containers.
correct_answer: Place durable records in a volume, database, or object store outside the replaceable container layer.
Reach the backend through its service name or internal address on the shared container network.

questions.text: Which statements describe distinct API security responsibilities correctly?
options: Authentication establishes or verifies the identity associated with an incoming API request.
Authorization determines which resources and actions an authenticated identity may use.
CORS replaces authentication whenever the caller is JavaScript running in a browser.
Input validation rejects malformed or disallowed data before business operations execute.
TLS assigns application roles after it encrypts traffic between the client and server.
Frontend JavaScript can safely contain permanent administrator keys when minified before deployment.
correct_answer: Authentication establishes or verifies the identity associated with an incoming API request.
Authorization determines which resources and actions an authenticated identity may use.
Input validation rejects malformed or disallowed data before business operations execute.

questions.text: Six months after deployment, an auditor asks the team to reproduce a model training run. Which records are most necessary?
options: Record an immutable dataset location or version together with a cryptographic checksum of the complete input.
Retain a descriptive workstation filename together with the timestamp when the analyst last opened it.
Record the Git commit and dependency lockfile or equivalent environment version for the run.
Save a screenshot of the leaderboard together with the model name shown in the interface.
Record a latest-data pointer so every reproduction attempt uses the newest corrected input automatically.
Record training parameters, random seed, and the train-validation split definition used for the original run.
Preserve model weights and deployment date without retaining the dataset or code versions that produced them.
Tie evaluation metrics and model artifact to the same immutable experiment run identifier for the release.
correct_answer: Record an immutable dataset location or version together with a cryptographic checksum of the complete input.
Record the Git commit and dependency lockfile or equivalent environment version for the run.
Record training parameters, random seed, and the train-validation split definition used for the original run.
Tie evaluation metrics and model artifact to the same immutable experiment run identifier for the release.

Inscript Pick the five most decision-useful context cards, give them in the order you would feed the AI, then name one uncertainty that still remains. At 10:30 AM a manager asks: “Checkout conversion collapsed after Checkout v3 went live. Did v3 cause it? Should we roll back now?” You intend to give this question to an AI. But you may provide the AI exactly five of the following twelve context cards. Your objective is not to give it “more context”. Your objective is to give it the most decision-useful context . Context cards A — Deployment record Checkout v3 was deployed to 100% of Web, Android, and iOS traffic at 10:00 AM. No other checkout application release occurred between 8:00 AM and 10:30 AM. B — Analytics migration note The iOS version of Checkout v3 renamed the successful-purchase analytics event from [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p15_Im1.webp|inline] to [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p15_Im2.webp|inline] . The production conversion dashboard still counts only [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p15_Im3.webp|inline] . C — Dashboard conversion by platform Four hours before → first 30 minutes after deployment: • Web: 3.1% → 3.0% • Android: 2.9% → 2.8% • iOS: 3.3% → 1.4% D — Payment backend Completed paid orders / checkout starts over the same periods: • Web: 3.0% → 3.0% • Android: 2.8% → 2.8% • iOS: 3.2% → 3.1% These figures come from the payment database, not analytics events. E — Support tickets Eleven checkout-related tickets arrived after 10:00 AM: seven mention coupon confusion, two mention a payment spinner, and two mention a declined card. Platform is not recorded. F — Marketing campaign A campaign beginning at 9:00 AM increased iOS visits by approximately 40%. Web and Android traffic were almost unchanged. G — Rollback policy A rollback takes approximately 30 minutes and may abandon carts currently in progress. Product policy says emergency rollback is appropriate for evidence of actual transaction or revenue harm, not merely an analytics-reporting defect. H — QA report Immediately before launch, 50 scripted payments across Web, Android, and iOS all completed successfully. I — Code review Checkout v3 changed approximately 1,240 lines of application code. J — Competitor news A competing retailer reported a payment outage yesterday. K — Historical variability On normal days, iOS conversion measured over 30-minute windows varies by roughly ±0.4 percentage points. L — Product lead message The product lead wrote: “Please don't roll this back during launch week unless we absolutely have to.” Your task Choose exactly five cards. Submit them in the order in which you would give them to the AI. Then state one important uncertainty that remains even after your five cards . Submit [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p17_Im1.webp|block] NOTE: Your answer should not exceed 60 words. Inscript Write the five questions you would ask the project owner before the team commits to building this system, each with what you would do differently depending on the answer. You receive this project brief: “Build a model that predicts which students will fail the end-term. Score everyone two days before the examination and email the 1,000 highest-risk students. Last term, 18% of students did not receive a passing grade. We have demographics, assignment scores, login history, forum activity, and exam-registration data. We should aim for at least 90% prediction accuracy.” Engineering is ready to start. You are allowed to ask the project owner only five questions before the team commits to building this system . The best question is not necessarily a technical question. It is a question whose answer could materially change: • whether the project should be done; • what should be built; • how it should be evaluated; • when it should run; • whom it should affect; • or what action should follow. Your task Write exactly five questions. For each question, briefly state what you would do differently depending on the answer . Do not answer your own questions. Submit [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p19_Im1.webp|block] NOTE: Your answer should not exceed 400 words. Max Word Count : 400 Min Word Count : 0 Highlight min word : Yes Single Line Response : No Number of Rows : 10 Number Of Columns : 70

Inscript An AI will repeatedly be asked to analyse small pilot experiments like the one below. Your job is not to answer the business question . Your job is to design a rubric capable of detecting bad AI answers. Business question given to the AI “Which onboarding variant, if any, should we expand into a larger controlled pilot?” Management's rule is: 1. Paid conversion must be higher than Control. 2. Support-ticket rate must be no more than 1.0 percentage point above Control . 3. The current pilot was not randomized . Individual branches chose which variant to use. [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p20_Im1.webp|block] Future AI answers may contain arithmetic errors, use the wrong denominator, ignore management rules, overstate what the evidence proves, or make other mistakes. Your task Create exactly five rubric checks an evaluator could apply to an AI's answer. A good rubric check is: • specific enough that two evaluators should usually agree; • checkable from the supplied task and data; • capable of rejecting a plausible but wrong answer; • not merely “the answer should be correct”. For each check provide: [IMAGE: /data/images/se2002_2026T2_ET_FN_p21_Im1.webp|block] Maximum 60 words per check. NOTE: Your answer should not exceed 400 words. Inscript Choose exactly three of the AI's claims to investigate before release and, for each, give the first manual check and why it is a priority. This is a follow-up to Q36 , not a new scenario. Use the same AI report and the risk assessment you completed there. Do not repeat the probability/impact table.
